newsitem.title: GERMANY: Helaba quits bank joint venture project.
newsitem.headline: Helaba quits bank joint venture project.

text.p: Helaba Landesbank Hessen-Thueringen, a German regional bank, said on Thursday it was pulling out of a project to set up a joint securities settlement company with two other regional banks.
Helaba said in a statement it had decided not to set up a joint venture with Suedwestdeutsche Landesbank and Bayerische Landesbank because of differences over which settlement system to use.
The publicly-owned banks are central clearing banks for the savings banks in the southern German states of Hesse, Thuringia, Bavaria and Baden-Wuerttemberg.

The planned bank, to be called Wertpapierbank-Sued, was to have carried out bourse transactions on behalf of the savings banks and hold customers' securities on deposit for them. The aim was to save costs.
It was not intended to trade in securities on its own account or to act as a fund management firm.
It was not immediately clear whether the other two banks planned to proceed with the project.
